title: Wren and the Landfall
premise: Beatrix Nakamura has spent a decade keeping her salvage crew small, quiet, and off the charts—until Vesper Kaine, her late mother's oldest rival, buys their debt and forces them to race the corporate fleet to the Meridian, a wreck sealed inside a tidewater glacier that Beatrix's mother died trying to reach. The job is personal in ways Kaine doesn't know: the Meridian holds both the inheritance Beatrix's mother left her and proof of what really happened the night she drowned. As tides narrow and the calving season looms, Beatrix must choose between protecting her crew's loyalty and unearthing a truth that will burn every bridge back home. In the end she beats the fleet by one tide, claims the truth over the treasure, and lets the glacier take the rest.
about_author: Quentin Villalobos is a former deckhand turned novelist who writes adventure stories set in cold water and colder silences. He lives on a converted trawler with his dog, Buoy, and an unhealthy collection of tide tables.

chapters.title: The Debt Comes Ashore
chapters.summary: Beatrix Nakamura's POV. Her crew finishes a quiet, profitable recovery off the Sound when a lawyer arrives with papers: their boat is collateral on a debt sold to Vesper Kaine. The beat is dread—the life Beatrix built to stay invisible just got foreclosed.

chapters.title: Terms of the Wreck
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Kaine offers forgiveness of the debt for one job: the Meridian, the wreck Beatrix's mother died chasing. Beatrix refuses; her first mate Okafor quietly signs anyway to save the crew's wages. Beat: betrayal dressed as loyalty.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. He lays out the math: six usable tides before calving season opens then closes the glacial route, and the corporate fleet is already provisioning. The crew votes, badly split. Beat: reluctant commitment under pressure.

chapters.title: What Mother Left in the Charts
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Going through her mother's old survey charts, Beatrix finds annotations in her own childhood handwriting she doesn't remember making—a route, a warning, a name. Beat: memory as unreliable inheritance.

chapters.title: Cold Water Crew
chapters.summary: POV of Junie, the young diver. Character chapter: the crew's dynamics, banter, and fractures as they provision. Junie idolizes Beatrix and senses the fear beneath her competence. Beat: warmth before the storm.

chapters.title: The Fleet at Anchor
chapters.summary: Kaine's POV. Aboard the corporate tender, Kaine watches Beatrix's boat slip past and reflects on the rivalry, the drowning, and what she actually wants from the Meridian—not gold but vindication. Beat: antagonist humanized, motives complicated.

chapters.title: First Tide: The Ice Gate
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The crew threads the ice-choked approach; near-disaster with a growler forces improvisation and cements trust. They find the gate exactly where the childhood annotations said it would be. Beat: awe laced with unease.

chapters.title: Echoes in the Hull
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. First dive on the Meridian's exposed superstructure. Junie finds fresh cutting marks—someone has been here recently, illegally. Beat: they are not alone, and not first.

chapters.title: The Ghost Diver
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Night watch; a light moves on the ice. Okafor confronts a scavenger who turns out to be a former crew member Beatrix exiled years ago, now working for the fleet. Beat: the past has employees.

chapters.title: Second Tide: The Sealed Hold
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. They breach the hold and find her mother's personal strongbox—unopened, addressed to Beatrix—alongside cargo manifests that contradict the official sinking report. Beat: grief interrupted by suspicion.

chapters.title: Manifest Lies
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, reading by lamplight. The manifests suggest the Meridian was scuttled deliberately, and her mother knew. Beatrix hides this from the crew. Beat: the loyalty-vs-truth theme turns inward.

chapters.title: Third Tide: Calving Warning
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The glacier groans; a minor calving nearly crushes the dive skiff. One crew member wants out; Okafor talks them down. Beat: stakes made physical, clock tightened to three tides.

chapters.title: Kaine's Confession, Half Of It
chapters.summary: Kaine's POV. Kaine boards under flag of truce, reveals she and Beatrix's mother were partners before the falling-out, and offers Beatrix the truth in exchange for the strongbox. Beatrix refuses. Beat: two inheritances colliding.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide: The Captain's Cabin
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Deep penetration dive to the captain's cabin; Beatrix finds her mother's logbook describing the scuttling order—and naming who gave it. The page is water-damaged at the crucial name. Beat: truth within reach, maddeningly blurred.

chapters.title: Fracture Line
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Okafor discovers Beatrix hid the manifests and confronts her; the crew overhears. Trust cracks along old fault lines. Beat: midpoint collapse—loyalty wounded by protective lies.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide: The Fleet Moves Early
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The corporate fleet enters the ice gate ahead of schedule, using the exiled diver's knowledge. A standoff on the ice ends in an uneasy, armed truce: both crews will lose everything if the calving comes early. Beat: enemies forced into shared peril.

chapters.title: The Name in the Water
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Working from memory instead of the damaged log, Beatrix reconstructs the annotation trail from her childhood dives and realizes the name was her mother's own—the scuttle was her mother's choice, to bury something worse than treasure. Beat: devastating reframe of grief.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide: The Race
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Final tide. Both crews dive simultaneously as the glacier begins to fail. Kaine goes deep against orders, chasing vindication. Beat: full-throttle climax, everything converging.

chapters.title: What the Glacier Keeps
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The calving begins. Beatrix abandons the prize cargo to drag Kaine from the collapsing wreck, losing the evidence that would clear or condemn anyone. Beat: choosing a life over a truth, at cost.

chapters.title: Aftermath on Open Water
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The boats limp out; the fleet withdraws; Kaine, humbled and indebted, voids the debt without being asked. The crew reckons with what Beatrix hid and forgives imperfectly. Beat: bruised reconciliation.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Alone, Beatrix finally opens her mother's strongbox: no fortune, only letters—one to Beatrix, one to Kaine, admitting everything. She sends Kaine hers. Beat: truth delivered gently, too late to hurt.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The crew makes landfall at their home harbor, charted anew with the Meridian marked honestly on the map. Beatrix chooses to stop hiding—registering the find, telling the story aloud. Beat: resolution; memory claimed, loyalty repaired, the wilderness remembered.
